q: I ran systemctl start myapp. Will it start again after a reboot?
expl: Start means now, enable means at boot, and they are independent. `enable --now` does both in one step.

q: How do I see the logs of one service since the last boot?
expl: `-b` is the current boot, `-u` picks the unit. `journalctl -f` alone follows the logs of everything and never ends by itself.
ch: 3. Logs since boot, or the last minutes

q: The `report` service failed. Type the `journalctl` command that shows only its last 5 log lines.
expl: `-u` picks the unit, `-n 5` keeps the last five lines. That's where the real reason is: the program doesn't exist.

q: `notes-app` is stopped and disabled. Type one `systemctl` command that starts it now AND makes it start at every boot.
expl: `enable --now` = enable (at boot) + start (now). Either one alone does only half of the job.

q: `web-app` is stopped. You run `systemctl enable web-app`. Is it running now?
expl: Enable just creates the boot link. The service stays inactive until you start it (or use `enable --now`).
opts: No: enable only sets it up for boot; use `enable --now` or `start`

q: `report.service` failed when we started it (its program doesn't exist). What does this print?
expl: A unit whose last run failed stays in the `failed` state (the red `×` in `systemctl status`) until you start it again or reset it.

q: Which command shows only messages with error level or worse from the last 10 minutes?
expl: `--since` takes a time in plain words and `-p err` keeps error, critical, alert and emergency. `-n 10` means ten lines, not minutes.

q: In the output of `systemctl status hello-app`, which line tells you whether the service is running?
expl: `Active: active (running)` means it runs; a broken one shows `Active: failed`. `Loaded:` only says where the unit file is and if it's enabled.

q: Type the `systemctl` command that tells you whether `hello-app` will start at boot (it prints enabled or disabled).
expl: `is-enabled` answers "at boot?", `is-active` answers "running now?". They are separate questions.
